evidence.source: 中華民國教育部《異體字字典》
evidence.text: The dictionary gives the received Shuowen analysis “論也。从言，吾聲” and lists the Analects use “子不語：怪、力、亂、神” under the sense “speak, discuss.” It separately records the Analects “居，吾語女” as “tell.” This supports distinct attested uses, but the dictionary does not date the composition or surviving witness of those texts.
evidence.title: [A03833] 語 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: 國學大師字形演變資料
evidence.field: 字形演變；古文字字形說明
evidence.text: The page records bronze exemplars indexed as 集成184 and 集成2840, Warring States examples from 郭店 and Qin slips including 睡虎地語15, followed by Shuowen seal script, Han clerical examples, regular script, and simplified form. Its account says the first bronze phonetic looks like a complex form of 五, the second is 吾; from Warring States script onward the analysis is 言 plus 吾 as phonetic. This complicates the simplified account of a single stable phonetic shape. The page’s exemplars and sequence do not establish the original referent or naming of the early phonetic shape.
evidence.title: 語字形演变字源 - 国学大师

evidence.source: 《說文解字》 text as reproduced in Wiktionary’s 言 entry
evidence.text: The entry reproduces Xu Shen’s distinction “直言曰言，論難曰語” and his analysis of 言 as 从口䇂聲. This is the Han dictionary’s semantic distinction between 言 and 語, not by itself proof of their earliest separate spoken senses or a complete graphic history.
evidence.title: 言 - 维基词典

evidence.source: 《简化字总表》（1986年版; text of the official 1964 joint notice reproduced at Wikisource）
evidence.field: 关于简化字的联合通知；《简化字总表》说明
evidence.text: The notice lists 讠 among simplified radicals and states that the 言 radical is generally simplified in left-side position. The table explains that parentheses give the original traditional form. Together with the Ministry entry’s analysis of 語 as 言 + 吾, this supports classifying traditional 言 → visible 讠 in 语 as simplified_form; it does not make 讠 an ancient component or establish an earlier ancestor.
evidence.title: 简化字总表（1986年版）

evidence.field: 字源；讀音；上古及中古讀音
evidence.text: The entry reports Modern Standard Mandarin pinyin yǔ and Cantonese Jyutping jyu5. For 語 it reports Baxter–Sagart 2014 OC *ŋ(r)aʔ, MC ngjoX, gloss “speak”; for the separate yù “tell” reading it gives OC *ŋ(r)aʔ-s, MC ngjoH. It also reports Zhengzhang Shangfang OC *ŋaʔ and *ŋas for the two readings. These are system-specific reconstructions, not directly observed ancient pronunciations.
evidence.title: 語 - 维基词典

evidence.field: 字源；讀音；上古及中古讀音
evidence.text: The entry gives standard Mandarin wú (with wǔ as a common variant), Cantonese ng4, Baxter–Sagart 2014 OC *ŋˤa and MC ngu, and Zhengzhang Shangfang OC *ŋaː. The local Baxter–Sagart table row independently checked for 吾 gives *ŋˤa, not the Zhengzhang value. Compare that Baxter–Sagart host reading with 語 *ŋ(r)aʔ cautiously: the reconstructions are similar enough to support a historical phonetic relationship, while their notation differs and modern Mandarin wú versus yǔ does not show that ancient relationship.
evidence.title: 吾 - 维基词典

evidence.field: 字源；發音；中古讀音；上古聲符系列
evidence.text: The entry gives Modern Standard Mandarin yán, Cantonese Jyutping jin4, Baxter-style Middle Chinese ngjon and Zhengzhang Shangfang OC *ŋan for 言. It lists the distinction attributed to Shuowen, “直言曰言，論難曰語.” These readings confirm the current pronunciation of the semantic component; they do not independently prove that 言 was selected for its meaning in 語, which is supported by the traditional component analysis and speech-related definition.
evidence.title: 言 - 维基词典

evidence.source: 中央研究院漢字資料庫
evidence.text: The inspected 吾 record identifies U+543E and gives modern readings wu2, yu2, ya2, alongside definitions including first-person pronoun “I.” This is current dictionary metadata and provides no ancient pronunciation evidence. The record was inspected for the semantic and phonetic host independently of 語.
evidence.title: 漢字「吾」：基本資料

evidence.source: 中央研究院漢字資料庫
evidence.text: The database’s documentation says its evolution view records ancient graph forms and graphic original meanings. The specific 語 evolution page opened during this research returned no readable content, so no glyph image was visually inspected and no claim here relies on visual inspection of that page.
evidence.title: 使用說明 - 漢字資料庫

gaps: No opened source established the earliest surviving written lexical occurrence of 語. The bronze page identifies Spring and Autumn and Warring States inscription witnesses, but this research did not verify an inscription context showing the word’s sense; do not present a dictionary gloss or later classical quotation as the chronologically first sense.

The Analects examples show ‘speak/discuss’ and ‘tell’ as separate early textual uses, but the Ministry dictionary does not date the extant witnesses; composition date and earliest surviving manuscript date remain distinct unresolved questions.

The bronze source reports an initial phonetic graph shaped as a complex 五 form and another as 吾; neither the source nor inspected evidence establishes the first shape’s original referent or pronunciation independently. The later phonetic analysis as 吾 is supported separately by the graph tradition and historical reading comparisons.

A proposed derivation of 言 from 語 plus nominal -n is attributed on Wiktionary to Schuessler (2007), but the supporting discussion was not independently inspected; keep it as a secondary proposal, not established history.

Local sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt rows were checked for 語 yǔ, 语 yǔ, 吾 wú, 言 yán, and 讠 yán; local Baxter–Sagart rows were checked for 語 (*ŋ(r)aʔ; *ŋ(r)aʔ-s), 吾 (*ŋˤa), and 言 (*ŋa[n] entries). The local paths are not external sources. Exact official Unicode per-character Unihan pages were attempted but could not be opened, so those local rows are not presented as externally verified evidence or linked as citations.

For current reading evidence, opened character-specific Wiktionary entries were used: 語 yǔ, 吾 wú, and 言 yán. The simplified 语 and positional component 讠 exact official Unicode Unihan records could not be verified; no host reading is substituted for a component reading.

No bulk extract is recommended: the inspected sources are character-specific or official standardization text, and no clear permission and editorial case for maintaining a local copied extract was established.
